name: Early returns below expectation ('what am I doing wrong?')
why: Groww owns the returns screen: how XIRR/absolute/negative values are framed for a 3-9 month SIP, and what context is shown. No fund advice needed.

name: My specific fund is lagging: stay, stop or switch?
why: Can show neutral benchmark/category context and 'what switching costs' facts, but cannot tell users which fund to hold.

name: SIP mechanics fail: mandate, debit-but-rejected, skip/modify/cancel flows
why: Entirely platform-controlled: mandate setup, failed-debit recovery, skip/pause UX, status messaging.

name: Money movement & account issues: redemption delays, bank change, KYC
why: Mostly ops + status transparency; partly AMC/RTA dependent.

name: App can't show my portfolio clearly (bugs, updates, external MF sync)
why: Product/engineering controlled; drives platform switching more than SIP stopping.

name: SIP vs real-life cash flow: salary, expenses, loans, emergency fund
why: Product can make SIP amount/date/skip fit income patterns (right-sizing at start, flexible skip instead of cancel). Income itself is outside control.

name: Which funds should I start with? (pre-start / first-month validation seeking)
why: Core need is fund choice, which we are not allowed to recommend; only process education (horizon, risk, number of funds) is possible.

name: Portfolio tinkering: too many funds, overlap, reshuffling
why: Can surface overlap/number-of-funds facts neutrally; churn often ends a SIP even when the investor keeps investing elsewhere.

name: Vernacular beginners: basic doubts ('can I lose principal?', missed instalment)
why: Plain-language Hindi/Hinglish explanations of how SIPs behave are fully in product control; fund-pick requests must be declined.

name: Chasing the hot asset (gold/silver/ETFs) instead of the running SIP
why: Driven by market narratives; product can only avoid amplifying it.
